column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline rule actions for the AutoPWN Suite dashboard.
# status as a failed gate: FAIL (exit 1) and every rule that is not listed here
# (reported as WARN, exit 2, i.e. "not triaged yet") both block the release.
# Only IGNORE entries below pass, and each one carries a written justification.
# Rules that ZAP reports as PASS need no entry.
# Triaged against real scans of the unauthenticated surface (login page and
# redirects) and an authenticated pass (dashboard, static assets, API GETs).
# Re-triaged after the dashboard added CSP, Permissions-Policy, COOP/COEP/CORP headers,
# a single Server header and POST forms; a headless Firefox confirmed it still loads under them.
# --- Hardening rules that now PASS: kept as FAIL so a regression blocks the release ---

column3: Content-Security-Policy must be present on every response
COEP/COOP/CORP cross-origin isolation headers must be present
Server header must not disclose Werkzeug/Python versions (the server now reports only AutoPWN-Suite)
No credentials or other sensitive data in URLs; the sign-in form now uses method=post

column1: # --- Informational or false positives, each justified ---

column3: CSP unsafe-inline (script-src and style-src): accepted for now because modules/web_ui_static/index.html still has inline on* event handlers and style attributes that need it; the sign-in page and every unauthenticated response (302/401/404) get a strict policy with no unsafe-inline, only authenticated dashboard pages get the lax one, and it is limited to same-origin with object-src 'none', base-uri 'none' and frame-ancestors 'none'. Remove this entry when the inline handlers are moved into app.js so the dashboard policy can be tightened

Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens: false positive for this design; the dashboard has no form-token CSRF defence by design. Every non-GET request needs the X-CSRF-Token header (bound to the session or sign-in challenge), SameSite=Strict cookies and a same-origin Origin check, enforced in before_request in modules/web_auth.py (covered by tests/unit/test_web_auth.py). The HTML forms (sign-in, account) are no-script fallbacks and the real requests are fetch calls with that header; ZAP's own form submission to /api/auth/account was rejected with 403 in the authenticated crawl. Caveat: ZAP only looks for a token field, so this rule cannot catch a future form that bypasses the header check; rely on the CSRF unit tests for that
Private IP Disclosure: false positive; 192.168.1.0 and 10.0.0.1 are example CIDR/target placeholders in the scan form and in web_security.js, not leaked addresses
Suspicious Comments: false positive; the matched word is "user" in ordinary explanatory comments in app.js and web_security.js
Non-Storable Content: intentional; every dashboard response sends Cache-Control: no-store because responses are private and per-session
Modern Web Application: informational notice that the page is script-driven; not a vulnerability
Authentication Request Identified: informational detection of the login form; not a vulnerability
